10. But with regard to this, the lower appellate Court observed as follows" "In this connection, it is to be noted that the plaintiff called for all necessary papers to prove his jote right from the ex-landlord. It was argued by the learned lawyer for the plaintiff that he called for all papers relating to disputed lands from the ex-landlord but none were produced and the non production of these documents by the defendants would lead us to presume that the plaintiffs had tenancy right in the suit land, observed by the learned lower Court." The learned Subordinate Judge without noticing the subsequent line of observation of the learned Munsif, it appears that he took the alleged presumption of the tenancy right of the plaintiff in the suit land as urged by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff to be an acceptance of the said right by the trial Court. Thus from an analysis of the facts and circumsatnces of the case and the materials on records I am of the opinion that the judgment of the Court of appeal below is not a proper judgment of reversal anal the same should be set aside. In view of the above, on setting aside the impugned judgment and decree, the appeal is generally sent back on remand to the Court of appeal below for rehearing and fresh decision in accordance with law, but as it is a very old suit of the year 1966 and when all materials are available on record, I feel that in the interest of justice this Court should exercise its jurisdiction under section 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure and decide the issues involved in the suit or the appeal on consideration of the materials on record. And this view of mine finds support from the decisions in the case of Khandakar Mohiuddin Vs. Syed Moin Ahmed reported in 28 DLR SC 85 and in the case Ajufannessa @ Aji Bibi and others Vs. Safar Miah and ors. reported in 30 DLR (SC) 41 and also in the case of Md. Altafur Rahman Vs. Tantijur Rahman reported in 30 DLR (SC) 236. In that view of the matter, I therefore want to decide the appeal afresh on consideration of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 12. Now, I have to see only which court is correct in deciding the question of title of the plaintiff over the suit-lands. It is contended by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent that the contesting defendant has failed to prove its plea that the suit-property vested in the Government and the Government got khas possession of the same from the ex-rent-receiver. It appears that in order to prove vesting of the suit property in the Government the defendant has produced Ext. A a certified copy of the order-sheet of the vesting case along with the list of excess lands of the ex-rent-receiver and examined a Tahsildar of the Tashil office as DW 1 and no other document has been filed in the Court in proof of vesting. Mr. SK Sinha, the learned Advocate submits that the defendant has failed to prove the vesting of the suit property, particularly when the Gazettee Notification in this connection has not been filed by the contesting defendant. The learned Advocate for the appellant on the other hand submits that by a Gazettee Notification, the wholesale acquisition of the interest of all the rent receivers was made and the rent-receivers were asked to submit their lists of choice lands, but so far this suit-property is concerned, the ex-landlord did not make any choice as a result the same vested in the Government as excess land by operation of law. As regards the non production of the Gazettce notification, he however could not give satisfactory explanation. Be that as it may, whatsoever weakness there might be in the defendant's case, the plaintiff must prove his own case satisfactorily to obtain a decree. In that view of the matter, let. me see how far the plaintiff has been able to prove his title in the suit lands. Admittedly, the plaintiff could not file any document of tide save and except Ext. I, of course he has led some oral evidence also, but those relate to his possession and not to his alleged claim of title in the suit-lands. As regards his other documents, it has been observed by the Court of Appeal below to the effect that "Besides these, certified copies of the order-sheet, judgment and plaint of other criminal cases and title suits are filed but they will not be of much help to the plaintiff." In finding title in favour of the plaintiff, a presumption has been tried to be drawn by the lower appellate Court in favour of the plaintiff's alleged tenancy right in the suitlands for alleged non-production of some documents by the defendants alleged to have been called for by the plaintiff from them. 

 13. The learned Advocate for the appellant however submits that nothing appears in the order-sheet of the trial Court that any such application was filed on behalf of the plaintiff calling for the alleged original documents from the defendants and that no officer of the Court of Wards Estate was cited as a witness to come to court with the original records of the said Estate. I have myself scrutinised the records and the order sheet of the suit but nothing is found in the order sheet. Only an application is found without any verification and without any date with a newly inserted page No. 22A citing the ex-rent receiver Abdur Reza Chowdhury and some other officers of the Court of Wards as witnesses. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellant that it was a spurious act of the plaintiff and he somehow inserted this application in the record in collusion with the office staff subsequently and it was not at all placed before the Court and hence no order was made thereon. The said application appears to have been written by a Moharar but neither his signature nor the signature of the Advocate concerned can be identified. Apart from that the impressed seal also appears to be unrecognizable and nothing can be read on the said seal. Thus the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant appears to be correct and no such application was actually presented before the Court in due course and hence no order was passed on the same. So, unless the ex-landlord or the staff or any officer of the Courts of Wards Estate as witness was summoned by the court asking him or them to produce the original documents a presumption of the tenancy-right in favour of the plaintiff in the suit-lands for non production of the same cannot bedrawn and this aspect of the matter has totally escaped the notice of both the courts below and as a result there has been a miscarriage of justice.
